_what: A DATED REFERENCE SNAPSHOT, checked in so the pinned FX table can be compared to something other than itself. The heartbeat's FX check (scan-heartbeat/index.ts) validates the pay filter against its own hand copy of the SAME pinned numbers, so it stays green at any drift: a consistency guard, not a freshness one. This file is the freshness half, and it is a snapshot with a date on it rather than a live fetch, because a test that calls the network fails on a plane and passes on a stale cache.
_source: https://api.frankfurter.dev/v1/latest?base=USD — ECB reference rates. Fetched 2026-09-26; the response's own date field said 2026-09-25 (the ECB publishes on business days, and 2026-09-26 was a Saturday).
_units: usdPerUnit = 1 / (units of that currency per USD), i.e. the same units as the CASE arms of salary_rank_usd, which multiply salary_min_annual by it.
_yardstick: A mid-market reference rate is the right yardstick for a magnitude-ranking column, and it is not the only defensible one. Drift figures computed from it are exact under this yardstick and would move a little under another.
